title: A component's definition
description: What every components/<name>/<name>.json says about its component. See PLAN.md.

purpose.description: What it is for, in a sentence or two.

proposed.description: Only for a component that isn't in the app today, such as one from future designs: where its design comes from. A component without it is in the app. Remove it if the component ships, and point its sources at the app.

design.description: Where the design comes from, such as a Figma file, or a screenshot of one until there's a link.

origin.description: Whether it is a native component, mirroring something native to the platform, or a GOV.UK app component, the app's own.

kind.description: native: a native component, which mirrors a platform control or pattern (a modal, a tab bar) and should behave as the platform's does. govuk: a GOV.UK app component, the app's own.

notes.description: What it is built on, and how it differs from the platform, if at all.

inputs.description: What it takes from the HTML that uses it.

content.description: What may be written between its tags, in words, or null if nothing. `contains` says the same as data.

parts.description: The elements that go only inside it, such as a grouped list's rows, by element name, each with its own attributes and contents.

outputs.description: What it tells the page. Components send no events of their own; these are the browser's events, from the controls it draws.

rules.description: How and when to use it, and when not to.

avoid.description: When it's the wrong choice, and what to use instead, so a designer, or a tool building a prototype, can choose between components that look alike or do similar things.

when.description: A situation it's the wrong choice for, such as For an action on the whole screen, such as Edit.

instead.description: What to use: an element of the library with any attributes it needs, as it's written in HTML, such as govuk-app-button variant="destructive", which the build checks; or, where nothing in the library fits, what to do, in words.

references.description: Screenshots of the app's own component, kept in the component's reference/ folder, to compare it with.

examples.description: Its states, as the HTML that draws them.

frame.description: What the docs draw it in. screen: a whole screen, phone height, with no padding of its own, for a component that lays out a screen. page: a box with room around it, the colour of a screen, for a component drawn on one, such as the search field. Otherwise a box with room around it, the colour of a modal.

attributes.description: The attributes it reads, by name. The build checks these are exactly the ones its script reads.

contains.description: What may go between its tags, as data, for tools that build pages from definitions, such as a prototype's schema. Empty if nothing may.

text.description: Text may go between its tags.

inline.description: Elements that may go inside its text, around a few words.

elements.description: Elements that may go between its tags.

slots.description: Elements that may go in each of its named slots, given slot="name".

elements.description: Which elements: those listed, or "any" of the library's components, which doesn't include another component's parts.

element.description: An element of the library, such as govuk-app-grouped-list-row.

part.description: An element that goes only inside its component, such as a grouped list's row.
